correctness.rationale: The local nine-case edge-form identity d_C=3d_G+h(v)-h(u), h=[0,-2,-1], telescopes on cycles and applies GLS Theorem 3. Distinct u-v path sums are independently counted by trinomial A_li(t_i) conditional on equal endpoint residue; all simple cycles are two-path unions. Their maximum mean gives the exact distribution and equal-length inclusion-exclusion. Independent direct enumeration of initial colourings matched every coefficient for (2,2,2), (2,3,3), (3,3,3). Trinomial variance 2/3, lattice local CLT and Riemann summation yield correct sharp constant; standard multivariate CLT gives rate limit.

value.rationale: Generalized theta graphs are a canonical multi-route network with a natural complete asymptotic-rate observable. An explicit distribution for every size, tractable equal-arm formula and sharp rare-synchronization and Gaussian-range limits are useful, not routine consequences of a graph-general maximum-cycle formula without path-sum enumeration.

final_claim: For any r>=3 internally disjoint u-v paths of lengths li>=2, three-color CCA and GHM have activities alpha_C=3 alpha_G for each initial colouring. The entire labelled activity-rate distribution is 3 sum over equal-mod-3 path sums ti of product trinomial coefficients, grouped by max_{i<j}|ti-tj|/(li+lj). For equal arms the rates are 3k/(2n), and for proportional large arms synchronization has explicit n^(-(r-1)/2) constant and scaled rates converge to Gaussian weighted range.
limitations: Unindexed path-sum probability or theta synchronization enumerations may contain an equivalent formula.
